Use case: identity-preserve. Asset type: transparent game sprite atlas for the Refresh edition of Adventures of Pierre.
Reference image 1 is the original idle Pierre. Reference image 2 is the original right-running animation strip. Reference image 3 is the wall-grab pose. Preserve this exact charming character: small friendly French cartoon man, black beret swept to one side, big rounded peach face and nose, blue-and-white horizontal striped shirt, dark blue trousers, small brown shoes. Match his old proportions and recognizable face, not a replacement hero.
Primary request: a faithful higher-resolution PIXEL ART remaster with deliberate crisp square pixels, clean dark outline, carefully limited flat colors and restrained 2-tone pixel shading. About 4 times the original pixel detail, still unmistakably retro sprite art. No smooth vector illustration, no 3D, no painting, no blur.
Deliver ONE precisely organized atlas with FOUR equal-width columns and TWO equal-height rows, eight isolated full-body poses, on a genuinely transparent background. No drawn checkerboard, no labels, no text, no floor/shadow, no frames. Aim for a 1408 by 1024 image. Each cell must have a generous transparent margin; every pose entirely inside its cell, feet on the same baseline within each row, same character size and identity across all cells. The character should occupy about 70 percent of cell width and 75 percent of cell height.
Exact reading order left to right:
Top row: (1) neutral standing pose facing slightly right, both feet planted; (2) running RIGHT, left leg reaching forward and right leg back; (3) running RIGHT, passing pose with knees under torso; (4) running RIGHT, right leg reaching forward and left leg back.
Bottom row: (5) airborne rising RIGHT with bent knees and arms balancing; (6) airborne falling RIGHT, feet pointed down and arms slightly raised; (7) clinging to an invisible wall on his RIGHT, both hands reaching right, legs tucked, no wall drawn; (8) comic defeated sitting/slumped pose, beret retained, simple dizzy expression, nonviolent, same bottom baseline.
Critical constraints: all eight poses coherent, pixel-art outlines equally crisp and dark, transparent cutouts, no overlapping cells, no corgis or scenery. Keep the reference outfit, hat, and face.

Use case: identity-preserve. Asset type: transparent pixel-art corgi sprite atlas for Adventures of Pierre Refresh.
Reference 1 is the original corgi sprite (the actual small corgi is in the upper left of the transparent canvas). Preserve its recognizable long low orange-tan body, short legs, upright pointed ears, white muzzle/chest/belly, dark nose, tiny tail, and friendly alert expression.
Primary request: faithful higher-resolution PIXEL ART remaster, about four times the original detail. Crisp deliberate square pixels and dark clean outlines, a small flat-color palette, restrained 2-tone pixel shading. Keep the side-on platformer silhouette. Not a realistic dog, not smooth vector art, no painting, no blur.
Deliver ONE genuinely transparent atlas in a TWO-column TWO-row layout, four equally sized isolated sprites, facing RIGHT in every cell. Aim for 1024 by 768 pixels. Each cell has generous transparent margins, equal character size and identical body/head design, long body about 75 percent of the cell width and 55 percent of the cell height. All paws on the same ground baseline within each row. Sprite silhouettes entirely inside their own cell.
Reading order: top-left neutral standing with all four paws down; top-right walking contact with near front paw forward and near back paw back; bottom-left walking passing pose with near paws gathered beneath the body; bottom-right walking contact with near front paw back and near back paw forward.
No text, no frames, no props, no scenery, no shadows or ground, no drawn checkerboard. Keep the orange-and-white coloring, black outlines, side profile and slightly homemade charm of the original.
